newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Boots eyes Christmas cheer as profits rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Boots eyes Christmas cheer as profits rise.

text.p: British pharmacist and retailer Boots Co Plc on Thursday reported a 9.4 percent increase in first half profits and said it was looking forward to a good Christmas now shoppers appeared to have loosened their purse strings.

Pretax profits in the half year to September 30 rose to 239.2 million pounds ($392.6 million) from 218.7 million. Total sales increased 12 percent to 2.12. billion pounds from 1.89 billion. The dividend was up 8.8 percent to 6.2 pence a share.
Deputy chairman and chief executive Lord Blyth said he was encouraged by the first half performance.
"From out point of view they're a good set of results. They're allowing us to continue our investment programme as we'd planned -- we're quietly confident," he said by telephone.
Boots shares rose after the results, but then retreated in line with a sharp drop in the London stock market to stand at 615 pence.
Analysts said the results looked promising. "It was a strong set of results, at the top end of expectations," said one.
The main business Boots The Chemist increased profits by 12 percent to 184.0 million pounds and sales by 6.3 percent to 1.54 billion. Sales excluding new space were up 4.6 percent.
The retailer sought to allay fears that profits from its chemist chain would suffer if long-standing price regulation covering over-the-counter medicines was scrapped in the next 18 months.
In September, Britain's Office of Fair Trading moved to do away with the fixed price regulations, which cover headache pills, vitamins and cold remedies. A decision is not expected until late 1997.
Blyth said a price free-for-all would affect only a relatively small percentage of over-the-counter medicines,

"Less than five percent of Boots The Chemists' profits are represented by those products," he said. "As a threat to the profits of this business, frankly, despite all the furore on the subject, it is trivial."
He said Boots had faced price pressures in the past on sun screens, fragrances and condoms and had won market share.

A long-awaited upturn in the home improvement market helped DIY chain Do It All cut its losses to 3.7 million pounds from 9.6 million. Boots now owns the entire business after buying out joint venture partner W.H. Smith Group Plc in June.
Boots expected Do It All to be cash positive next year. "I would be very surprised if we don't have it in operating profit in the course of next year," Blyth said.
The group is ditching the poorly performing Do It All outlets and has around 50 left to sell, leaving it with a chain of about 133. Blyth said there were no current plans to sell the business.
He said integration of French skincare group Laboratoires Lusia, which Boots Healthcare International bought in September for 115 million pounds was going well.

The company was still on the look out for an over-the-counter healthcare business in Germany. "The big lacuna if you like continues to be Germany and we're struggling mightily to try and fill that but so are a lot of other people," he said.
Boots is also attempting to export its highly successful Boots The Chemist format outside Britain.
Its first store in Dublin opens on Friday and pilot stores are due to open in the Netherlands, Thailand and Japan. ($1=.6093 Pound)
